question: Which LP2-49–51 grid cells have a visually bare I/l stem, and how much can those ten case decisions change a conditional base-60 byte inventory?
scope: All 256 grid cells are retained. Only the ten listed I/l stem cells vary; the visually uppercase 2S at LP2-50 row 12 column 5 and every other cell stay at wiki transcription values.
visual_rule: On the preserved 2400 x 3600 seventh-onion JPEGs, these ten grid positions show a vertical stem with no visible dot or foot. Such a shape alone cannot distinguish uppercase I from lowercase l. This is a manual observation, not an OCR claim.
byte_rule: For a conditional representation only: 0-9 A-Z a-x map to digits 0-59 in that order; a two-character token is 60 times its first digit plus its second digit; require 0-255.
enumeration: Toggle I versus l independently at the ten fixed cells (2^10 = 1024 cases). Preserve source order and every other wiki token. Count distinct tokens, total one-bits across 256 bytes, and even-valued bytes for every case.
decision: Report exact source and wiki readings, both conditional byte values per stem, and the complete metric range. No candidate decoding or probability claim.
